The annual hurdle rates for the 2026 and 2025 calendar&#160;years, calculated as of the immediately preceding December&#160;31<span class="CharOverride-12" style="font-size:58%;vertical-align:super;">st</span>, were <ix:nonFraction contextRef="c323" decimals="4" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="oxsq:PreIncentiveFeeHurdleRate" scale="-2" unitRef="pure" id="ixv-24585">8.73</ix:nonFraction>% and <ix:nonFraction contextRef="c324" decimals="4" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="oxsq:PreIncentiveFeeHurdleRate" scale="-2" unitRef="pure" id="ixv-24586">9.38</ix:nonFraction>% respectively, under the terms of the Investment Advisory Agreement. The Company&#8217;s net investment income (to the extent not distributed to stockholders) used to calculate the Net Investment Income Incentive Fee was also included in the amount of gross assets used to calculate the <ix:nonFraction contextRef="c0" decimals="2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="us-gaap:PropertyManagementFeePercentFee" scale="-2" unitRef="pure" id="ixv-24587">2</ix:nonFraction>% Base Fee.</p>
		<p class="NL_m" style="margin:0;padding:0;border-width:0;font-family:Times New Roman PS Std, serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-variant:normal;font-weight:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:48pt;margin-right:0;margin-top:8pt;orphans:2;page-break-after:auto;page-break-before:auto;text-align:left;text-indent:-24pt;widows:3;margin-left:72pt;margin-top:8pt;">a.<span style="width: 20px;display: inline-block;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;</span>The operation of the incentive fee with respect to the Company&#8217;s Pre<span class="nobreak">-Incentive</span> Fee Net Investment Income for each quarter is as follows:</p>
		<p class="NL_m" style="margin:0;padding:0;border-width:0;font-family:Times New Roman PS Std, serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-variant:normal;font-weight:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:48pt;margin-right:0;margin-top:8pt;orphans:2;page-break-after:auto;page-break-before:auto;text-align:left;text-indent:-24pt;widows:3;margin-left:96pt;margin-top:8pt;">i.<span style="width: 23px;display: inline-block;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;</span>no incentive fee is payable to Oxford Square Management in any calendar quarter in which the Pre<span class="nobreak">-Incentive</span> Fee Net Investment Income does not exceed one fourth of the annual hurdle rate (<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c513" decimals="4" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="oxsq:PreIncentiveFeeHurdleRate" scale="-2" unitRef="pure" id="ixv-24588">8.73</ix:nonFraction>% for the 2026 calendar year).</p>
		<p class="NL_m" style="margin:0;padding:0;border-width:0;font-family:Times New Roman PS Std, serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-variant:normal;font-weight:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:48pt;margin-right:0;margin-top:8pt;orphans:2;page-break-after:auto;page-break-before:auto;text-align:left;text-indent:-24pt;widows:3;margin-left:96pt;margin-top:8pt;">ii.<span style="width: 20px;display: inline-block;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;</span><ix:nonFraction contextRef="c513" decimals="2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="oxsq:IncomeAdvisorIncentiveFeeRate" scale="-2" unitRef="pure" id="ixv-24589">20</ix:nonFraction>% of the amount of the Pre<span class="nobreak">-Incentive</span> Fee Net Investment Income, if any, that exceeds one<span class="nobreak">-fourth</span> of the annual hurdle rate (<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c514" decimals="4" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="oxsq:AnnualHurdleRate" scale="-2" unitRef="pure" id="ixv-24590">8.73</ix:nonFraction>% for the 2026 calendar year) in any calendar quarter is payable to Oxford Square Management (i.e., once the hurdle rate is reached, <ix:nonFraction contextRef="c515" decimals="2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="oxsq:PreIncentiveFeeNetInvestmentIncomeMaximumPercentage" scale="-2" unitRef="pure" id="ixv-24591">20</ix:nonFraction>% of all Pre<span class="nobreak">-Incentive</span> Fee Net Investment Income thereafter will be allocated to Oxford Square Management).</p>
		<p class="Text_ind" style="margin:0;padding:0;border-width:0;font-family:Times New Roman PS Std, serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-variant:normal;font-weight:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:8pt;orphans:2;page-break-after:auto;page-break-before:auto;text-align:left;text-indent:24pt;widows:3;margin-top:8pt;">Under the terms of the 2016 Fee Waiver, for the purpose of calculating the amount of total advisory fees (if any) to be waived during a particular calendar quarter, the Income Incentive Fee (as a portion of the total calculation) is calculated based on the amount by which (x)&#160;the &#8220;Pre<span class="nobreak">-Incentive</span> Fee Net Investment Income&#8221; (as defined above) for the calendar quarter exceeds (y)&#160;the &#8220;Preferred Return Amount&#8221; (as defined below) for the calendar quarter.</p>
		<p class="NL_m" style="margin:0;padding:0;border-width:0;font-family:Times New Roman PS Std, serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-variant:normal;font-weight:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:48pt;margin-right:0;margin-top:8pt;orphans:2;page-break-after:auto;page-break-before:auto;text-align:left;text-indent:-24pt;widows:3;margin-top:8pt;">a.<span style="width: 20px;display: inline-block;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;</span>A &#8220;Preferred Return Amount&#8221; is calculated on a quarterly basis by multiplying <ix:nonFraction contextRef="c0" decimals="4" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="oxsq:PreferredReturnAmountPercentage" scale="-2" unitRef="pure" id="ixv-24592">1.75</ix:nonFraction>% by the Company&#8217;s net asset value at the end of the immediately preceding calendar quarter.</p>

		<p class="NL_m" style="margin:0;padding:0;border-width:0;font-family:Times New Roman PS Std, serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-variant:normal;font-weight:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:48pt;margin-right:0;margin-top:8pt;orphans:2;page-break-after:auto;page-break-before:auto;text-align:left;text-indent:-24pt;widows:3;margin-left:72pt;margin-top:8pt;">(a)<span style="width: 17px;display: inline-block;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;</span>no Net Investment Income Incentive Fee is payable to Oxford Square Management in any calendar quarter in which the &#8220;Pre<span class="nobreak">-Incentive</span> Fee Net Investment Income&#8221; does not exceed the &#8220;Preferred Return Amount&#8221;;</p>

RELATED PARTY TRANSACTIONS<span class="CharOverride-1" style="font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;"> (cont.)</span></p>
		<ix:continuation continuedAt="_RelatedPartyTransactionsDisclosureTextBlock-c0_cont_4" id="_RelatedPartyTransactionsDisclosureTextBlock-c0_cont_3"><p class="NL_m" style="margin:0;padding:0;border-width:0;font-family:Times New Roman PS Std, serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-variant:normal;font-weight:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:48pt;margin-right:0;margin-top:8pt;orphans:2;page-break-after:auto;page-break-before:auto;text-align:left;text-indent:-24pt;widows:3;margin-top:8pt;">d.<span style="width: 20px;display: inline-block;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;</span>The calculation of the Company&#8217;s Net Investment Income Incentive Fee is subject to a total return requirement that provides that a Net Investment Income Incentive Fee will not be payable to Oxford Square Management except to the extent <ix:nonFraction contextRef="c7" decimals="2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="oxsq:PreIncentiveFeeNetInvestmentIncomeMaximumPercentage" scale="-2" unitRef="pure" id="ixv-24596">20</ix:nonFraction>% of the &#8220;cumulative net increase in net assets resulting from operations&#8221; (which is the amount, if positive, of the sum of the &#8220;Pre<span class="nobreak">-Incentive</span> Fee Net Investment Income,&#8221; realized gains and losses and unrealized appreciation and depreciation) during the calendar quarter for which such fees are being calculated and the eleven (11)&#160;preceding quarters exceeds the cumulative Net Investment Income Incentive Fees accrued and/or paid for such eleven (11)&#160;preceding quarters.</p>
		<p class="Text_ind" style="margin:0;padding:0;border-width:0;font-family:Times New Roman PS Std, serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-variant:normal;font-weight:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:8pt;orphans:2;page-break-after:auto;page-break-before:auto;text-align:left;text-indent:24pt;widows:3;margin-top:8pt;">In the event that the advisory fee calculations under the 2016 Fee Waiver produce a higher combined Base Fee and Net Investment Income Incentive Fee for any quarterly period, the combined fees are set to the original (lower) level, calculated pursuant to the Investment Advisory Agreement. In the event that advisory fee calculations under the 2016 Fee Wavier produce a lower combined Base Fee and Net Investment Income Incentive Fee for that quarterly period, those lower combined fees are adopted for that quarterly period. In either case, the lower level of combined fees is used for that quarter, and, accordingly, the advisory fee payable to Oxford Square Management can only be reduced, and never increased, as a result of the 2016 Fee Waiver.</p>

		<p class="H6" style="margin:0;padding:0;border-width:0;font-family:Times New Roman PS Std, serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-variant:normal;font-weight:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:12pt;orphans:1;page-break-after:avoid;page-break-before:auto;text-align:left;text-decoration:underline;text-indent:0;widows:1;margin-top:12pt;"><span class="CharOverride-11" style="text-decoration:underline;">Capital Gains Incentive Fee</span></p>
		<p class="Text_ind" style="margin:0;padding:0;border-width:0;font-family:Times New Roman PS Std, serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-variant:normal;font-weight:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:8pt;orphans:2;page-break-after:auto;page-break-before:auto;text-align:left;text-indent:24pt;widows:3;margin-top:8pt;">The Capital Gains Incentive Fee, which is calculated identically under the Investment Advisory Agreement and under the 2016 Fee Waiver, is determined and payable in arrears as of the end of each calendar year (or upon termination of the Investment Advisory Agreement, as of the termination date), and equals <ix:nonFraction contextRef="c511" decimals="2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="oxsq:IncentiveFeeOnCapitalGainsPercentage" scale="-2" unitRef="pure" id="ixv-24597">20</ix:nonFraction>% of the Company&#8217;s &#8220;Incentive Fee Capital Gains,&#8221; which consists of its realized capital gains for each calendar year, computed net of all realized capital losses and unrealized capital depreciation for that calendar year. For accounting purposes only, in order to reflect the theoretical Capital Gains Incentive Fee that would be payable for a given period as if all unrealized gains were realized, the Company will accrue a Capital Gains Incentive Fee based upon net realized gains and unrealized depreciation for that calendar year (in accordance with the terms of the Investment Advisory Agreement), plus unrealized appreciation on investments held at the end of the period. It should be noted that a fee so calculated and accrued would not necessarily be payable under the Investment Advisory Agreement, and may never be paid based upon the computation of Capital Gains Incentive Fees in subsequent periods. Amounts paid under the Investment Advisory Agreement will be consistent with the formula reflected in the Investment Advisory Agreement.</p>
		<p class="Text_ind" style="margin:0;padding:0;border-width:0;font-family:Times New Roman PS Std, serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-variant:normal;font-weight:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:8pt;orphans:2;page-break-after:auto;page-break-before:auto;text-align:left;text-indent:24pt;widows:3;margin-top:8pt;">The amount of Capital Gains Incentive Fee expense related to the hypothetical liquidation of the portfolio (and assuming no other changes in realized or unrealized gains and losses) would only become payable to Oxford Square Management in the event of a complete liquidation of the Company&#8217;s portfolio as of period end and the termination of the Investment Advisory Agreement on such date. Also, it should be noted that the Capital Gains Incentive Fee expense fluctuates with the Company&#8217;s overall investment results.</p></ix:continuation>

		<p class="H3" style="margin:0;padding:0;border-width:0;font-family:Times New Roman PS Std, serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-variant:normal;font-weight:bold;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:12pt;orphans:99;page-break-after:avoid;page-break-before:auto;text-align:left;text-indent:0;widows:1;margin-top:12pt;">Administration Agreement</p>
		<p class="Text_ind" style="margin:0;padding:0;border-width:0;font-family:Times New Roman PS Std, serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-variant:normal;font-weight:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:8pt;orphans:2;page-break-after:auto;page-break-before:auto;text-align:left;text-indent:24pt;widows:3;margin-top:8pt;">The Company has also entered into the Administration Agreement with Oxford Funds under which Oxford Funds provides administrative services for the Company. The Company pays Oxford Funds an allocable portion of overhead and other expenses incurred by Oxford Funds on its behalf under the Administration Agreement, including a portion of the rent and the compensation of the Chief Financial Officer, accounting staff and other administrative support personnel, which creates potential conflicts of interest that the Board must monitor. The Company also reimburses Oxford Funds for the costs associated with the functions performed by the Company&#8217;s Chief Compliance Officer that Oxford Funds pays on the Company&#8217;s behalf pursuant to the terms of an agreement between the Company and ACA Group, LLC.</p>
		<p class="Text_ind" style="margin:0;padding:0;border-width:0;font-family:Times New Roman PS Std, serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-variant:normal;font-weight:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:8pt;orphans:2;page-break-after:auto;page-break-before:auto;text-align:left;text-indent:24pt;widows:3;margin-top:8pt;">Oxford Square Management is controlled by Oxford Funds, its managing member. Oxford Funds manages the business and internal affairs of Oxford Square Management. Jonathan H.&#160;Cohen, the Company&#8217;s Chief Executive Officer, as well as a Director, is the Chief Executive Officer of Oxford Square Management and managing member of Oxford Funds. Saul B.&#160;Rosenthal, the Company&#8217;s President and Chief Operating Officer, is also the President and Chief Operating Officer of Oxford Square Management and a member of Oxford Funds. Messrs. Cohen and Rosenthal together control the equity interests in Oxford Funds.</p>

In addition, the Company incurred approximately $<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c0" decimals="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="us-gaap:FacilityCosts" scale="0" unitRef="usd" id="ixv-24600">15,000</ix:nonFraction> and $<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c311" decimals="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="us-gaap:FacilityCosts" scale="0" unitRef="usd" id="ixv-24601">14,000</ix:nonFraction> for facility costs allocated under the Administration Agreement for the three&#160;months ended March&#160;31, 2026 and 2025, respectively. As of March&#160;31, 2026, approximately $<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c0" decimals="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="us-gaap:DefinedBenefitPlanAdministrationExpenses" scale="0" unitRef="usd" id="ixv-24602">77,000</ix:nonFraction> of accrued compensation expenses was payable under the Administration Agreement. As of December&#160;31, 2025, approximately $<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c454" decimals="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="us-gaap:DefinedBenefitPlanAdministrationExpenses" scale="0" unitRef="usd" id="ixv-24603">26,000</ix:nonFraction> of accrued compensation expenses was payable under the Administration Agreement.</p>
		<p class="H3" style="margin:0;padding:0;border-width:0;font-family:Times New Roman PS Std, serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-variant:normal;font-weight:bold;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:12pt;orphans:99;page-break-after:avoid;page-break-before:auto;text-align:left;text-indent:0;widows:1;margin-top:12pt;">Co-Investment Exemptive Relief</p>
		<p class="Text_ind" style="margin:0;padding:0;border-width:0;font-family:Times New Roman PS Std, serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-variant:normal;font-weight:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:8pt;orphans:2;page-break-after:auto;page-break-before:auto;text-align:left;text-indent:24pt;widows:3;margin-top:8pt;">On January&#160;6, 2026, the Company received an updated form of co<span class="nobreak">-investment</span> exemptive relief from the SEC to allow certain managed funds and investment vehicles, each of whose investment adviser is Oxford Square Management or an investment adviser controlling, controlled by or under common control with Oxford Square Management, to participate in negotiated co<span class="nobreak">-investment</span> transactions where doing so is consistent with regulatory requirements and other pertinent factors, and pursuant to the conditions of the exemptive relief (the &#8220;Co<span class="nobreak">-Investment</span> Order&#8221;). The Co<span class="nobreak">-Investment</span> Order, which supersedes the co<span class="nobreak">-investment</span> order issued to the Company on June&#160;14, 2017, is a new form of co<span class="nobreak">-investment</span> exemptive relief that adopts a more flexible requirement that allocations be &#8220;fair and equitable&#8221; to the Company and that Oxford Square Management considers the interests of the Company and other affiliated 1940 Act<span class="nobreak">-regulated</span> funds that rely on the Co<span class="nobreak">-Investment</span> Order in allocations and which minimizes certain board approval requirements as compared to the prior form of co<span class="nobreak">-investment</span> exemptive relief. Among other things, under the Co<span class="nobreak">-Investment</span> Order, the terms, conditions, price, class of securities to be purchased in respect of a particular investment, the date on which such investment is to be made and any registration rights applicable thereto, must be generally the same for the Company and each other participating affiliated entity. The requirements of the Co<span class="nobreak">-Investment</span> Order (including any requirements for board approval thereunder), as well as other regulatory requirements associated with the Company and other affiliated 1940 Act<span class="nobreak">-regulated</span> funds that rely on the Co<span class="nobreak">-Investment</span> Order, potentially will impact the investment allocations among participating entities </p></ix:continuation>

		<ix:nonNumeric contextRef="c0" continuedAt="oxsq_DistributionsTextBlock-c0_cont_1" escape="true" name="oxsq:DistributionsTextBlock" id="ixv-18491"><p class="H2" style="margin:0;padding:0;border-width:0;font-family:Times New Roman PS Std, serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-variant:normal;font-weight:bold;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:12pt;orphans:99;page-break-after:avoid;page-break-before:auto;text-align:left;text-indent:0;widows:1;margin-top:12pt;">NOTE 9. DISTRIBUTIONS</p>
		<p class="Text_ind" style="margin:0;padding:0;border-width:0;font-family:Times New Roman PS Std, serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-variant:normal;font-weight:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:8pt;orphans:2;page-break-after:auto;page-break-before:auto;text-align:left;text-indent:24pt;widows:3;margin-top:8pt;">The Company intends to continue to operate so as to qualify to be taxed as a RIC under the Code and, as such, the Company would not be subject to federal income tax on the portion of its taxable income and gains distributed to stockholders. To qualify to be taxed as a RIC, the Company is required, among other requirements, to distribute at least <ix:nonFraction contextRef="c0" decimals="2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="oxsq:PercentageOfDistributeMinimumAnnualInvestmentCompanyTaxableIncome" scale="-2" unitRef="pure" id="ixv-24614">90</ix:nonFraction>% of its annual investment company taxable income, as defined by the Code. The amount to be paid out as a distribution each quarter is determined by the Board and is based upon the annual taxable income estimated by the management of the Company. Income calculated in accordance with U.S.&#160;federal income tax regulations differs substantially from GAAP income. To the extent that the Company&#8217;s cumulative undistributed taxable earnings fall below the amount of distributions declared, however, a portion of the total amount of the Company&#8217;s distributions for the fiscal year may be deemed a return of capital for tax purposes to the Company&#8217;s stockholders.</p>
		<p class="Text_ind" style="margin:0;padding:0;border-width:0;font-family:Times New Roman PS Std, serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-variant:normal;font-weight:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:8pt;orphans:2;page-break-after:auto;page-break-before:auto;text-align:left;text-indent:24pt;widows:3;margin-top:8pt;">The Company intends to comply with the applicable provisions of the Code pertaining to RICs to make distributions of taxable income sufficient to relieve it of substantially all federal income taxes. The Company, at its discretion, may carry forward taxable income in excess of calendar year distributions and pay a <ix:nonFraction contextRef="c0" decimals="2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="oxsq:ExciseTaxPercentage" scale="-2" unitRef="pure" id="ixv-24615">4</ix:nonFraction>% excise tax on such income. The Company will accrue excise tax on estimated excess taxable income, if any, as required. The Company has accrued approximately $<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c7" decimals="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="us-gaap:SalesAndExciseTaxPayableCurrentAndNoncurrent" scale="0" unitRef="usd" id="ixv-24616">524,000</ix:nonFraction> of estimated excise tax payable for estimated excise tax on undistributed taxable income as of March<span class="nobreak"> </span>31, 2026. This amount is included in &#8220;Accrued Expenses&#8221; on the Statements of Assets and Liabilities.</p>
		<p class="Text_ind" style="margin:0;padding:0;border-width:0;font-family:Times New Roman PS Std, serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-variant:normal;font-weight:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:8pt;orphans:2;page-break-after:auto;page-break-before:auto;text-align:left;text-indent:24pt;widows:3;margin-top:8pt;">The Company has adopted an &#8220;opt out&#8221; distribution reinvestment plan for its common stockholders. As a result, if the Company makes a cash distribution, then stockholders&#8217; cash distributions will be automatically reinvested in additional shares of its common stock, unless they specifically &#8220;opt out&#8221; of the distribution reinvestment plan so as to receive cash distributions. 		<ix:continuation id="oxsq_DistributionsTextBlock-c0_cont_1"><p class="Text_ind" style="margin:0;padding:0;border-width:0;font-family:Times New Roman PS Std, serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-variant:normal;font-weight:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:8pt;orphans:2;page-break-after:auto;page-break-before:auto;text-align:left;text-indent:24pt;widows:3;margin-top:8pt;">Under the Regulated Investment Company Modernization Act&#160;of&#160;2010 (the &#8220;Act&#8221;), the Company is permitted to carry forward capital losses incurred in taxable&#160;years beginning after the date of enactment for an unlimited period. However, any losses incurred during those future taxable&#160;years will be required to be utilized prior to the losses incurred in pre<span class="nobreak">-enactment</span> taxable&#160;years, which carry an expiration date. As a result of this ordering rule, pre<span class="nobreak">-enactment</span> capital loss carryforwards may be more likely to expire unused. Additionally, post<span class="nobreak">-enactment</span> capital losses that are carried forward will retain their character as either short<span class="nobreak">-term</span> or long<span class="nobreak">-term</span> losses rather than being considered all short<span class="nobreak">-term</span> as under previous law.</p>

For the three&#160;months ended March&#160;31, 2026 and 2025, the amounts and sources of distributions reported are only estimates (based on an average of the reported tax character historically) and are not being provided for U.S.&#160;federal income tax reporting purposes. The timing and character of distributions for U.S.&#160;federal income tax purposes (which are determined in accordance with the U.S.&#160;federal tax rules which may differ from GAAP) may be materially different than the historical information the Company used in providing the estimates herein. The ultimate tax character of distributions during 2026 and 2025 is unknown until the Company&#8217;s tax returns are filed, and the amounts represented may be materially different from the amounts disclosed in the final Form&#160;1099<span class="nobreak">-DIV</span> notices. To the extent the Company&#8217;s taxable earnings fall below the total amount of the Company&#8217;s distributions for that fiscal year, a portion of those distributions may be deemed a tax return of capital to the Company&#8217;s stockholders. The ultimate tax character of the Company&#8217;s earnings cannot be determined until tax returns are prepared after the end of the fiscal year. The amounts and sources of distributions reported are only estimates (based on an average of the reported tax character historically) and are not being provided for U.S.&#160;tax reporting purposes.</ix:footnote></p>

Total return is not annualized.</ix:footnote></p>

		<ix:nonNumeric contextRef="c0" escape="true" name="cef:InvestmentObjectivesAndPracticesTextBlock" id="ixv-19435"><p class="Text_ind" style="margin:0;padding:0;border-width:0;font-family:Times New Roman PS Std, serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-variant:normal;font-weight:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:8pt;orphans:2;page-break-after:auto;page-break-before:auto;text-align:left;text-indent:24pt;widows:3;margin-top:8pt;">Our investment objective is to maximize our portfolio&#8217;s total return. Our primary focus is to seek an attractive risk<span class="nobreak">-adjusted</span> total return by investing primarily in corporate debt securities and, to a lesser extent, in collateralized loan obligations (&#8220;CLO&#8221;), which are structured finance investments that own corporate debt securities. CLO investments may also include warehouse facilities, which are early<span class="nobreak">-stage</span> CLO vehicles intended to aggregate loans that may be used to form the basis of a traditional CLO vehicle. We operate as a closed<span class="nobreak">-end</span> management investment company and have elected to be regulated as a business development company (&#8220;BDC&#8221;) under the Investment Company Act&#160;of&#160;1940, as amended (the &#8220;1940 Act&#8221;). We have elected to be treated for tax purposes as a regulated investment company (&#8220;RIC&#8221;), under Subchapter M of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended (the &#8220;Code&#8221;).</p>
		<p class="Text_ind" style="margin:0;padding:0;border-width:0;font-family:Times New Roman PS Std, serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-variant:normal;font-weight:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:8pt;orphans:2;page-break-after:auto;page-break-before:auto;text-align:left;text-indent:24pt;widows:3;margin-top:8pt;">Our investment activities are managed by Oxford Square Management, LLC (&#8220;Oxford Square Management&#8221;), a registered investment adviser under the Investment Advisers Act&#160;of&#160;1940, as amended. Oxford Square Management is owned by Oxford Funds, LLC (&#8220;Oxford Funds&#8221;), its managing member, and a related party, Charles M.&#160;Royce, a member of our Board of Directors (&#8220;Board&#8221;) who holds a minority, non<span class="nobreak">-controlling</span> interest in Oxford Square Management. Jonathan H.&#160;Cohen, our Chief Executive Officer, and Saul B.&#160;Rosenthal, our President, are the controlling members of Oxford Funds. Under an investment advisory agreement (the &#8220;Investment Advisory Agreement&#8221;), we have agreed to pay Oxford Square Management an annual base management fee calculated on gross assets, and an incentive fee based upon our performance. Under an amended and restated administration agreement (the &#8220;Administration Agreement&#8221;), we have agreed to pay or reimburse Oxford Funds, as administrator, for certain expenses incurred in operating the Company. Our executive officers and directors, and the executive officers of Oxford Square Management and Oxford Funds, serve or may serve as officers and directors of entities that operate in a line of business similar to our own. Accordingly, they may have obligations to investors in those entities, the fulfillment of which might not be in the best interests of us or our stockholders.</p></ix:nonNumeric>

We expect that our investment portfolio will be diversified among a large number of investments with few investments, if any, exceeding 5.0% of the total portfolio. As of March&#160;31, 2026, our debt investments </p>

In addition, our total portfolio had a weighted average annualized yield on debt investments of approximately 14.74% as of March&#160;31, 2026.</p>
		<p class="Text_ind" style="margin:0;padding:0;border-width:0;font-family:Times New Roman PS Std, serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-variant:normal;font-weight:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:8pt;orphans:2;page-break-after:auto;page-break-before:auto;text-align:left;text-indent:24pt;widows:3;margin-top:8pt;">The weighted average annualized yield of our debt investments is not the same as a return on investment for our stockholders but, rather, relates to a portion of our investment portfolio and is calculated before the payment of all of our fees and expenses. The weighted average annualized yield was computed using the effective interest rates as of March&#160;31, 2026, including accretion of original issue discount (&#8220;OID&#8221;) and excluding any debt investments on non<span class="nobreak">-accrual</span> status. There can be no assurance that the weighted average annualized yield will remain at its current level.</p>
		<p class="Text_ind" style="margin:0;padding:0;border-width:0;font-family:Times New Roman PS Std, serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-variant:normal;font-weight:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:8pt;orphans:2;page-break-after:auto;page-break-before:auto;text-align:left;text-indent:24pt;widows:3;margin-top:8pt;">We have borrowed funds to make investments and may continue to borrow funds to make investments. As a result, we are exposed to the risks of leverage, which may be considered a speculative investment technique. Borrowings, also known as leverage, magnify the potential for gain and loss on amounts invested and therefore increase the risks associated with investing in our securities. In addition, the costs associated with our borrowings, including any increase in the management fees payable to Oxford Square Management, will be borne by our common stockholders.</p>
		<p class="Text_ind" style="margin:0;padding:0;border-width:0;font-family:Times New Roman PS Std, serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-variant:normal;font-weight:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:8pt;orphans:2;page-break-after:auto;page-break-before:auto;text-align:left;text-indent:24pt;widows:3;margin-top:8pt;">In addition, as a BDC under the 1940 Act, we are required to make available significant managerial assistance, for which we may receive fees, to our portfolio companies. This assistance could involve, among other things, monitoring the operations of our portfolio companies, participating in board and management meetings, consulting with and advising officers of portfolio companies and providing other organizational and financial guidance. These fees would be generally non<span class="nobreak">-recurring</span>, however in some instances they may have a recurring component. We have received no fee income for managerial assistance to date.</p>
		<p class="Text_ind" style="margin:0;padding:0;border-width:0;font-family:Times New Roman PS Std, serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-variant:normal;font-weight:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:8pt;orphans:2;page-break-after:auto;page-break-before:auto;text-align:left;text-indent:24pt;widows:3;margin-top:8pt;">To the extent possible, we will generally seek to invest in loans that are collateralized by a security interest in the borrower&#8217;s assets or guaranteed by a principal to the transaction. Interest payments, if not deferred, are normally payable quarterly with most debt investments having scheduled principal payments on a monthly or quarterly basis. When we receive a warrant to purchase stock in a portfolio company, the warrant will typically have a nominal strike price, and will entitle us to purchase a modest percentage of the borrower&#8217;s stock.</p>
		<p class="Text_ind" style="margin:0;padding:0;border-width:0;font-family:Times New Roman PS Std, serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-variant:normal;font-weight:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:8pt;orphans:2;page-break-after:auto;page-break-before:auto;text-align:left;text-indent:24pt;widows:3;margin-top:8pt;">During the three&#160;months ended March&#160;31, 2026, U.S.&#160;loan market performance weakened versus the prior quarter. U.S.&#160;loan prices, as defined by the Morningstar/LSTA US Leveraged Loan Index, decreased from 96.64% of par as of December&#160;31, 2025 to 94.63% of par as of March&#160;31, 2026.</p>
		<p class="Text_ind" style="margin:0;padding:0;border-width:0;font-family:Times New Roman PS Std, serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-variant:normal;font-weight:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:8pt;orphans:2;page-break-after:auto;page-break-before:auto;text-align:left;text-indent:24pt;widows:3;margin-top:8pt;">As of March&#160;31, 2026, the Company&#8217;s Board of Directors approved the fair value of the Company&#8217;s investment portfolio of approximately $235.4&#160;million in good faith in accordance with the Company&#8217;s valuation procedures.</p>
		<p class="H2" style="margin:0;padding:0;border-width:0;font-family:Times New Roman PS Std, serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-variant:normal;font-weight:bold;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:12pt;orphans:99;page-break-after:avoid;page-break-before:auto;text-align:left;text-indent:0;widows:1;margin-top:12pt;"><span class="Bold" style="font-style:normal;font-weight:bold;">CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES</span></p>
		<p class="Text_ind" style="margin:0;padding:0;border-width:0;font-family:Times New Roman PS Std, serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-variant:normal;font-weight:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:8pt;orphans:2;page-break-after:auto;page-break-before:auto;text-align:left;text-indent:24pt;widows:3;margin-top:8pt;">The preparation of financial statements and related disclosures in conformity with generally accepted accounting principles in the United&#160;States (&#8220;GAAP&#8221;) requires management to make estimates and assumptions that affect (i)&#160;the reported amounts of assets and liabilities, (ii)&#160;disclosure of contingent assets and liabilities at the date of the financial statements, and (iii)&#160;revenues and expenses during the periods reported. Our critical accounting estimates, including those relating to the valuation of our investment portfolio, are described below. Actual results could materially differ from those estimates. The critical accounting estimates should be read in conjunction with our risk factors as disclosed in <span class="Italic" style="font-style:italic;font-weight:normal;">Item&#160;1A.&#160;&#8212;&#160;Risk Factors</span> contained in our Annual Report on Form&#160;10<span class="nobreak">-K</span> for the year ended December&#160;31, 2025. See &#8220;Note&#160;3. Summary of Significant Accounting Policies&#8221; to our financial statements for the three&#160;months ended March&#160;31, 2026 for more information on our critical accounting policies.</p>
		<p class="H2" style="margin:0;padding:0;border-width:0;font-family:Times New Roman PS Std, serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-variant:normal;font-weight:bold;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:12pt;orphans:99;page-break-after:avoid;page-break-before:auto;text-align:left;text-indent:0;widows:1;margin-top:12pt;"><span class="Bold" style="font-style:normal;font-weight:bold;">Investment Valuation</span></p>
		<p class="Text_ind" style="margin:0;padding:0;border-width:0;font-family:Times New Roman PS Std, serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-variant:normal;font-weight:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:8pt;orphans:2;page-break-after:auto;page-break-before:auto;text-align:left;text-indent:24pt;widows:3;margin-top:8pt;">Our Board of Directors determines the fair value of our investment portfolio in accordance with the provisions of ASC&#160;820, <span class="Italic" style="font-style:italic;font-weight:normal;">Fair Value Measurement and Disclosure</span> (&#8220;ASC&#160;820&#8221;) and Rule&#160;2a<span class="nobreak">-5</span> under the 1940 Act. Estimates made in the preparation of our financial<span class="Italic" style="font-style:italic;font-weight:normal;"> </span>statements include the valuation of investments and the related amounts of unrealized appreciation and depreciation of investments recorded. We believe that there is no single definitive method for determining fair value. As a result, determining fair value requires that judgment be applied to the specific facts and circumstances of each portfolio investment while employing a consistently applied valuation process for the types of investments we make.</p>

	<div class="_idGenObjectStyleOverride-1" style="margin:0;padding:0;border-width:0;border-width:0pt;">
		<p class="Text_ind" style="margin:0;padding:0;border-width:0;font-family:Times New Roman PS Std, serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-variant:normal;font-weight:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:8pt;orphans:2;page-break-after:auto;page-break-before:auto;text-align:left;text-indent:24pt;widows:3;margin-top:8pt;margin-top:7.5pt;">ASC&#160;820 clarifies the definition of fair value and requires companies to expand their disclosure about the use of fair value to measure assets and liabilities in interim and annual periods subsequent to initial recognition.</p>
		<p class="Text_ind" style="margin:0;padding:0;border-width:0;font-family:Times New Roman PS Std, serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-variant:normal;font-weight:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:8pt;orphans:2;page-break-after:auto;page-break-before:auto;text-align:left;text-indent:24pt;widows:3;margin-top:8pt;margin-top:7.5pt;">ASC&#160;820 defines fair value as the price that would be received to sell an asset or paid to transfer a liability in an orderly transaction between market participants at the measurement date. ASC&#160;820 also establishes a three<span class="nobreak">-tier</span> fair value hierarchy, which prioritizes the inputs used in measuring fair value. These tiers include:</p>
		<p class="BL_m" style="margin:0;padding:0;border-width:0;font-family:Times New Roman PS Std, serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-variant:normal;font-weight:normal;list-style-position:outside;list-style-type:disc;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:48pt;margin-right:0;margin-top:8pt;orphans:2;page-break-after:auto;page-break-before:auto;text-align:left;text-indent:-24pt;widows:3;margin-top:8pt;margin-top:7.5pt;"><span class="bullet" style="font-size:10pt;">&#8226;<span style="width: 27px;display: inline-block;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;</span></span>Level<span class="nobreak"> </span>1, defined as observable inputs such as quoted prices in active markets;</p>
		<p class="BL_m" style="margin:0;padding:0;border-width:0;font-family:Times New Roman PS Std, serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-variant:normal;font-weight:normal;list-style-position:outside;list-style-type:disc;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:48pt;margin-right:0;margin-top:8pt;orphans:2;page-break-after:auto;page-break-before:auto;text-align:left;text-indent:-24pt;widows:3;margin-top:8pt;margin-top:7.5pt;"><span class="bullet" style="font-size:10pt;">&#8226;<span style="width: 27px;display: inline-block;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;</span></span>Level<span class="nobreak"> </span>2, which includes inputs such as quoted prices for similar securities in active markets and quoted prices for identical securities in markets that are not active; and</p>
		<p class="BL_m" style="margin:0;padding:0;border-width:0;font-family:Times New Roman PS Std, serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-variant:normal;font-weight:normal;list-style-position:outside;list-style-type:disc;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:48pt;margin-right:0;margin-top:8pt;orphans:2;page-break-after:auto;page-break-before:auto;text-align:left;text-indent:-24pt;widows:3;margin-top:8pt;margin-top:7.5pt;"><span class="bullet" style="font-size:10pt;">&#8226;<span style="width: 27px;display: inline-block;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;</span></span>Level<span class="nobreak"> </span>3, defined as unobservable inputs for which little or no market data exists, therefore requiring an entity to develop its own assumptions.</p>
		<p class="Text_ind" style="margin:0;padding:0;border-width:0;font-family:Times New Roman PS Std, serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-variant:normal;font-weight:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:8pt;orphans:2;page-break-after:auto;page-break-before:auto;text-align:left;text-indent:24pt;widows:3;margin-top:8pt;margin-top:7.5pt;">We consider the attributes of current market conditions on an on<span class="nobreak">-going</span> basis and have determined that due to the general illiquidity of the market for our investment portfolio, whereby little or no market data exists, substantially all of our fair valued investments are measured based upon Level 3 inputs as of March&#160;31, 2026 and December&#160;31, 2025.</p>
		<p class="Text_ind" style="margin:0;padding:0;border-width:0;font-family:Times New Roman PS Std, serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-variant:normal;font-weight:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:8pt;orphans:2;page-break-after:auto;page-break-before:auto;text-align:left;text-indent:24pt;widows:3;margin-top:8pt;margin-top:7.5pt;">Our Board of Directors determines the value of our investment portfolio each quarter. In connection with that determination, members of Oxford Square Management&#8217;s portfolio management team prepare a quarterly analysis of each portfolio investment using the most recent portfolio company financial statements, forecasts and other relevant financial and operational information. We may elect to value a recently purchased investment at cost. We&#160;may also engage a third<span class="nobreak">-party</span> valuation firm to provide assistance in valuing certain of our syndicated loans and bilateral investments, including related equity investments, although our Board of Directors ultimately determines the appropriate valuation of each such investment. Changes in fair value, as described above, are recorded in the statements of operations as net change in unrealized appreciation/depreciation.</p>
		<p class="Text_ind" style="margin:0;padding:0;border-width:0;font-family:Times New Roman PS Std, serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-variant:normal;font-weight:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:8pt;orphans:2;page-break-after:auto;page-break-before:auto;text-align:left;text-indent:24pt;widows:3;margin-top:8pt;margin-top:7.5pt;">Our corporate loan portfolio investments are valued using several valuation processes. The quantitative inputs and data points that determine which method to utilize to value any given investment include, but are not limited to:</p>
		<p class="BL_m" style="margin:0;padding:0;border-width:0;font-family:Times New Roman PS Std, serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-variant:normal;font-weight:normal;list-style-position:outside;list-style-type:disc;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:48pt;margin-right:0;margin-top:8pt;orphans:2;page-break-after:auto;page-break-before:auto;text-align:left;text-indent:-24pt;widows:3;margin-top:8pt;margin-top:7.5pt;"><span class="bullet" style="font-size:10pt;">&#8226;<span style="width: 27px;display: inline-block;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;</span></span>Bid/offer prices;</p>
		<p class="BL_m" style="margin:0;padding:0;border-width:0;font-family:Times New Roman PS Std, serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-variant:normal;font-weight:normal;list-style-position:outside;list-style-type:disc;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:48pt;margin-right:0;margin-top:8pt;orphans:2;page-break-after:auto;page-break-before:auto;text-align:left;text-indent:-24pt;widows:3;margin-top:8pt;margin-top:7.5pt;"><span class="bullet" style="font-size:10pt;">&#8226;<span style="width: 27px;display: inline-block;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;</span></span>Depth, which is defined as the number of securities firms that make a market in a respective corporate syndicated loan and contribute data on the corporate syndicated loan to market data providers;</p>
		<p class="BL_m" style="margin:0;padding:0;border-width:0;font-family:Times New Roman PS Std, serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-variant:normal;font-weight:normal;list-style-position:outside;list-style-type:disc;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:48pt;margin-right:0;margin-top:8pt;orphans:2;page-break-after:auto;page-break-before:auto;text-align:left;text-indent:-24pt;widows:3;margin-top:8pt;margin-top:7.5pt;"><span class="bullet" style="font-size:10pt;">&#8226;<span style="width: 27px;display: inline-block;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;</span></span>Liquidity score, which is a metric to help market participants ascertain their ability to exit a position within a given time frame and near a prevailing indicative price, which provides a benchmark of liquidity risk;</p>
		<p class="BL_m" style="margin:0;padding:0;border-width:0;font-family:Times New Roman PS Std, serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-variant:normal;font-weight:normal;list-style-position:outside;list-style-type:disc;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:48pt;margin-right:0;margin-top:8pt;orphans:2;page-break-after:auto;page-break-before:auto;text-align:left;text-indent:-24pt;widows:3;margin-top:8pt;margin-top:7.5pt;"><span class="bullet" style="font-size:10pt;">&#8226;<span style="width: 27px;display: inline-block;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;</span></span>Financial performance of the underlying portfolio company;</p>
		<p class="BL_m" style="margin:0;padding:0;border-width:0;font-family:Times New Roman PS Std, serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-variant:normal;font-weight:normal;list-style-position:outside;list-style-type:disc;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:48pt;margin-right:0;margin-top:8pt;orphans:2;page-break-after:auto;page-break-before:auto;text-align:left;text-indent:-24pt;widows:3;margin-top:8pt;margin-top:7.5pt;"><span class="bullet" style="font-size:10pt;">&#8226;<span style="width: 27px;display: inline-block;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;</span></span>Recent business developments;</p>
		<p class="BL_m" style="margin:0;padding:0;border-width:0;font-family:Times New Roman PS Std, serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-variant:normal;font-weight:normal;list-style-position:outside;list-style-type:disc;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:48pt;margin-right:0;margin-top:8pt;orphans:2;page-break-after:auto;page-break-before:auto;text-align:left;text-indent:-24pt;widows:3;margin-top:8pt;margin-top:7.5pt;"><span class="bullet" style="font-size:10pt;">&#8226;<span style="width: 27px;display: inline-block;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;</span></span>Covenant compliance; and</p>
		<p class="BL_m" style="margin:0;padding:0;border-width:0;font-family:Times New Roman PS Std, serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-variant:normal;font-weight:normal;list-style-position:outside;list-style-type:disc;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:48pt;margin-right:0;margin-top:8pt;orphans:2;page-break-after:auto;page-break-before:auto;text-align:left;text-indent:-24pt;widows:3;margin-top:8pt;margin-top:7.5pt;"><span class="bullet" style="font-size:10pt;">&#8226;<span style="width: 27px;display: inline-block;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;</span></span>Recent transactions.</p>
		<p class="Text_ind" style="margin:0;padding:0;border-width:0;font-family:Times New Roman PS Std, serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-variant:normal;font-weight:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:8pt;orphans:2;page-break-after:auto;page-break-before:auto;text-align:left;text-indent:24pt;widows:3;margin-top:8pt;margin-top:7.5pt;">In instances where secondary market data is limited, we may engage a third<span class="nobreak">-party</span> valuation firm to independently determine an estimate of fair value. Currently, we have a single company valued via a third<span class="nobreak">-party</span> valuation firm. This valuation method employs a waterfall method whereby the enterprise value (&#8220;EV&#8221;) of the company is estimated based on company financial performance inputs, such as EBITDA, and publicly traded comparable company multiples. The EV is then attributed to each debt tranche, preferred equity tranche, and common equity, in order of seniority, to arrive at a valuation for our holdings. Generally speaking, as estimated EV increases, the fair value of our investments will also increase. As market multiples and EBITDA increase, estimated EV will also increase.</p>
		<p class="Text_ind" style="margin:0;padding:0;border-width:0;font-family:Times New Roman PS Std, serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-variant:normal;font-weight:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:8pt;orphans:2;page-break-after:auto;page-break-before:auto;text-align:left;text-indent:24pt;widows:3;margin-top:8pt;margin-top:7.5pt;">In valuing our CLO debt and equity investments, we consider the indicative prices provided by a recognized industry pricing service as a primary source, and the implied yield of such prices, supplemented by actual trades executed in the market at or around period<span class="nobreak">-end</span>, as well as the indicative prices provided by brokers who arrange transactions in such investment vehicles. We also consider those instances in which the record date for an equity distribution payment falls on the last&#160;day of the period, and the likelihood that a prospective purchaser would require </p>
		</div>

		<p class="RRH" style="margin:0;padding:0;border-width:0;font-family:Times New Roman PS Std, serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-variant:normal;font-weight:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:0;orphans:1;page-break-after:auto;page-break-before:auto;text-align:center;text-indent:0;widows:1;margin: 10px 0px 10px 0pt; page-break-after: always; border-bottom: 1px solid; margin-top: 10.0pt; margin-right: 0in; margin-bottom: 10.0pt; margin-left: 0in; text-align: center; font-size: 10.0pt; font-family: Times New Roman PS Std, serif; color: black;">47</p>
		<p class="Text_flush" style="margin:0;padding:0;border-width:0;font-family:Times New Roman PS Std, serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-variant:normal;font-weight:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:8pt;orphans:2;page-break-after:auto;page-break-before:auto;text-align:left;text-indent:0;widows:2;margin-top:8pt;"><a href="#TOC001">Table of Contents</a></p>



	<div class="_idGenObjectStyleOverride-1" style="margin:0;padding:0;border-width:0;border-width:0pt;">
		<p class="Text_ind" style="margin:0;padding:0;border-width:0;font-family:Times New Roman PS Std, serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-variant:normal;font-weight:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:8pt;orphans:2;page-break-after:auto;page-break-before:auto;text-align:left;text-indent:24pt;widows:3;margin-top:8pt;text-indent:0;margin-top:7.5pt;">a downward adjustment to the indicative price representing substantially all of the pending distribution. Additional factors include any available information on other relevant transactions including firm bids and offers in the market and information resulting from bids<span class="nobreak">-wanted-in-competition</span>. In addition, we consider the operating metrics of the specific investment vehicle, including compliance with collateralization tests, defaulted and restructured securities, and payment defaults, if any. We calculate the fair value of certain CLO equity investments based upon the net present value of expected contractual payment streams discounted using estimated market yields for the equity tranche of the respective CLO vehicle. Oxford Square Management or its Valuation Committee may request an additional analysis by a third<span class="nobreak">-party</span> firm to assist in the valuation process of CLO investment vehicles. All information is presented to our Board for its determination of fair value of these investments.</p>
		<p class="H3" style="margin:0;padding:0;border-width:0;font-family:Times New Roman PS Std, serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-variant:normal;font-weight:bold;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:12pt;orphans:99;page-break-after:avoid;page-break-before:auto;text-align:left;text-indent:0;widows:1;margin-top:12pt;"><span class="BoldItalic" style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Recently Issued Accounting Standards</span></p>
		<p class="Text_ind" style="margin:0;padding:0;border-width:0;font-family:Times New Roman PS Std, serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-variant:normal;font-weight:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:8pt;orphans:2;page-break-after:auto;page-break-before:auto;text-align:left;text-indent:24pt;widows:3;margin-top:8pt;">See &#8220;Note&#160;3. Summary of Significant Accounting Policies&#8221; to our financial statements for a description of recent accounting pronouncements, including the impact on our financial statements.</p>
		<p class="H2" style="margin:0;padding:0;border-width:0;font-family:Times New Roman PS Std, serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-variant:normal;font-weight:bold;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:12pt;orphans:99;page-break-after:avoid;page-break-before:auto;text-align:left;text-indent:0;widows:1;margin-top:12pt;"><span class="Bold" style="font-style:normal;font-weight:bold;">PORTFOLIO COMPOSITION AND INVESTMENT ACTIVITY</span></p>
		<p class="Text_ind" style="margin:0;padding:0;border-width:0;font-family:Times New Roman PS Std, serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-variant:normal;font-weight:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:8pt;orphans:2;page-break-after:auto;page-break-before:auto;text-align:left;text-indent:24pt;widows:3;margin-top:8pt;">The total fair value of our investment portfolio was approximately $235.4&#160;million and $251.7&#160;million as of March&#160;31, 2026, and December&#160;31, 2025, respectively. The decrease in the value of investments during the three month period ended March&#160;31, 2026, was due primarily to net realized losses of approximately $30.7&#160;million, and debt repayments of approximately $0.4&#160;million, which were partially offset by investment acquisitions of approximately $15.8&#160;million and net unrealized appreciation on our investment portfolio of approximately $1.1&#160;million (which incorporates reductions to CLO equity cost value of $3.9&#160;million).</p>
		<p class="Text_ind" style="margin:0;padding:0;border-width:0;font-family:Times New Roman PS Std, serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-variant:normal;font-weight:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:8pt;orphans:2;page-break-after:auto;page-break-before:auto;text-align:left;text-indent:24pt;widows:3;margin-top:8pt;">A reconciliation of the investment portfolio for the three&#160;months ended March&#160;31, 2026 and the year ended December&#160;31, 2025 follows:</p>

		<p class="Text_ind" style="margin:0;padding:0;border-width:0;font-family:Times New Roman PS Std, serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-variant:normal;font-weight:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:8pt;orphans:2;page-break-after:auto;page-break-before:auto;text-align:left;text-indent:24pt;widows:3;margin-top:8pt;">Interest expense for the three&#160;months ended March&#160;31, 2026, was approximately $2.8&#160;million, which primarily relates to our 5.50% unsecured notes due 2028 (the &#8220;5.50% Unsecured Notes&#8221;) and 7.75% unsecured notes due 2030 (the &#8220;7.75% Unsecured Notes&#8221;). Interest expense for the three&#160;months ended March&#160;31, 2025, was approximately $2.0&#160;million, which primarily relates to our 5.50% Unsecured Notes and 6.25% unsecured notes due 2026 (the &#8220;6.25% Unsecured Notes&#8221;).</p>
		<p class="Text_ind" style="margin:0;padding:0;border-width:0;font-family:Times New Roman PS Std, serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-variant:normal;font-weight:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:8pt;orphans:2;page-break-after:auto;page-break-before:auto;text-align:left;text-indent:24pt;widows:3;margin-top:8pt;">Professional fees, consisting of legal, consulting, valuation, audit and tax services, were approximately $347,000 for the three&#160;months ended March&#160;31, 2026, compared to approximately $323,000 for the three&#160;months ended March&#160;31, 2025. That increase for the three&#160;months ended March&#160;31, 2026 was primarily due to higher legal fees, partially offset by lower consulting fees.</p>
		<p class="Text_ind" style="margin:0;padding:0;border-width:0;font-family:Times New Roman PS Std, serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-variant:normal;font-weight:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:8pt;orphans:2;page-break-after:auto;page-break-before:auto;text-align:left;text-indent:24pt;widows:3;margin-top:8pt;">Compensation expense was approximately $247,000 for the three&#160;months ended March&#160;31, 2026, compared to approximately $240,000 for the three&#160;months ended March&#160;31, 2025. Compensation expense reflects the allocation of compensation expenses for the services of our Chief Financial Officer, accounting personnel, and other administrative support staff.</p>
		<p class="Text_ind" style="margin:0;padding:0;border-width:0;font-family:Times New Roman PS Std, serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-variant:normal;font-weight:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:8pt;orphans:2;page-break-after:auto;page-break-before:auto;text-align:left;text-indent:24pt;widows:3;margin-top:8pt;">General and administrative expenses, consisting primarily of directors&#8217; fees, insurance, listing fees, transfer agent and custodian fees, market data services, facilities costs and other expenses, was approximately $313,000 for the three&#160;months ended March&#160;31, 2026, compared to approximately $355,000 for the three&#160;months ended March&#160;31, 2025. Office supplies, facilities costs and other expenses are allocated to us under the terms of the Administration Agreement.</p>
		<p class="Text_ind" style="margin:0;padding:0;border-width:0;font-family:Times New Roman PS Std, serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-variant:normal;font-weight:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:8pt;orphans:2;page-break-after:auto;page-break-before:auto;text-align:left;text-indent:24pt;widows:3;margin-top:8pt;">Excise tax was approximately $105,000 for the three&#160;months ended March&#160;31, 2026, compared to approximately $121,000 for the three&#160;months ended March&#160;31, 2025.</p>

		<p class="LRH" style="margin:0;padding:0;border-width:0;font-family:Times New Roman PS Std, serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-variant:normal;font-weight:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:0;orphans:1;page-break-after:auto;page-break-before:auto;text-align:center;text-indent:0;widows:1;margin: 10px 0px 10px 0pt; page-break-after: always; border-bottom: 1px solid; margin-top: 10.0pt; margin-right: 0in; margin-bottom: 10.0pt; margin-left: 0in; text-align: center; font-size: 10.0pt; font-family: Times New Roman PS Std, serif; color: black;">52</p>
		<p class="Text_flush" style="margin:0;padding:0;border-width:0;font-family:Times New Roman PS Std, serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-variant:normal;font-weight:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:8pt;orphans:2;page-break-after:auto;page-break-before:auto;text-align:left;text-indent:0;widows:2;margin-top:8pt;"><a href="#TOC001">Table of Contents</a></p>



	<div class="_idGenObjectStyleOverride-1" style="margin:0;padding:0;border-width:0;border-width:0pt;">
		<p class="H4" style="margin:0;padding:0;border-width:0;font-family:Times New Roman PS Std, serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-variant:normal;font-weight:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:12pt;orphans:1;page-break-after:avoid;page-break-before:auto;text-align:left;text-indent:0;widows:1;margin-top:12pt;"><span class="Italic" style="font-style:italic;font-weight:normal;">Incentive Fees</span></p>
		<p class="Text_ind" style="margin:0;padding:0;border-width:0;font-family:Times New Roman PS Std, serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-variant:normal;font-weight:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:8pt;orphans:2;page-break-after:auto;page-break-before:auto;text-align:left;text-indent:24pt;widows:3;margin-top:8pt;">There was no net investment income incentive fee (&#8220;Net Investment Income Incentive Fee&#8221;) recorded for the three&#160;months ended March&#160;31, 2026 and 2025. The Net Investment Income Incentive Fee is calculated and payable quarterly in arrears based on the amount by which (x)&#160;the &#8220;Pre<span class="nobreak">-Incentive</span> Fee Net Investment Income&#8221; for the immediately preceding calendar quarter exceeds (y)&#160;the &#8220;Preferred Return Amount&#8221; for the calendar quarter. For this purpose, &#8220;Pre<span class="nobreak">-Incentive</span> Fee Net Investment Income&#8221; means interest income, dividend income and any other income accrued during the calendar quarter minus our operating expenses for the quarter (including the Base Fee, expenses payable under the Administration Agreement with Oxford Funds, and any interest expense and dividends paid on any issued and outstanding preferred stock, but excluding the incentive fee). Refer to &#8220;Note&#160;7. Related Party Transactions&#8221; in the notes to our financial statements.</p>
		<p class="Text_ind" style="margin:0;padding:0;border-width:0;font-family:Times New Roman PS Std, serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-variant:normal;font-weight:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:8pt;orphans:2;page-break-after:auto;page-break-before:auto;text-align:left;text-indent:24pt;widows:3;margin-top:8pt;">The expense attributable to the capital gains incentive fee (the &#8220;Capital Gains Incentive Fee&#8221;), as reported under GAAP, is calculated as if the Company&#8217;s entire portfolio had been liquidated at period end, and therefore is calculated on the basis of net realized and unrealized gains and losses at the end of each period. That expense (or the reversal of such an expense) related to that hypothetical liquidation of the portfolio (and assuming no other changes in realized or unrealized gains and losses) would only become payable to our investment adviser in the event of a complete liquidation of our portfolio as of period end and the termination of the Investment Advisory Agreement on such date. For the three&#160;months ended March&#160;31, 2026 and 2025, no accrual was required as a result of the impact of accumulated net unrealized depreciation and net realized losses on our portfolio.</p>
		<p class="Text_ind" style="margin:0;padding:0;border-width:0;font-family:Times New Roman PS Std, serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-variant:normal;font-weight:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:8pt;orphans:2;page-break-after:auto;page-break-before:auto;text-align:left;text-indent:24pt;widows:3;margin-top:8pt;">The amount of the Capital Gains Incentive Fee which will actually be payable is determined in accordance with the terms of the Investment Advisory Agreement and is calculated as of the end of each calendar year (or upon termination of the Investment Advisory Agreement). The terms of the Investment Advisory Agreement state that the Capital Gains Incentive Fee calculation is based on net realized gains, if any, offset by gross unrealized depreciation for the calendar year. No effect is given to gross unrealized appreciation in this calculation. For the three&#160;months ended March&#160;31, 2026 and 2025, such an accrual was not required under the terms of the Investment Advisory Agreement.</p>
		<p class="H2" style="margin:0;padding:0;border-width:0;font-family:Times New Roman PS Std, serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-variant:normal;font-weight:bold;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:12pt;orphans:99;page-break-after:avoid;page-break-before:auto;text-align:left;text-indent:0;widows:1;margin-top:12pt;"><span class="Bold" style="font-style:normal;font-weight:bold;">Realized and Unrealized Gains/Losses on Investments</span></p>
		<p class="Text_ind" style="margin:0;padding:0;border-width:0;font-family:Times New Roman PS Std, serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-variant:normal;font-weight:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:8pt;orphans:2;page-break-after:auto;page-break-before:auto;text-align:left;text-indent:24pt;widows:3;margin-top:8pt;">For the three&#160;months ended March&#160;31, 2026, we recognized net realized losses of approximately $30.7&#160;million, which were primarily attributable to a restructuring of a senior secured loan and an extinguishment of a CLO equity position.</p>
		<p class="Text_ind" style="margin:0;padding:0;border-width:0;font-family:Times New Roman PS Std, serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-variant:normal;font-weight:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:8pt;orphans:2;page-break-after:auto;page-break-before:auto;text-align:left;text-indent:24pt;widows:3;margin-top:8pt;">For the three&#160;months ended March&#160;31, 2026, our net change in unrealized appreciation was approximately $1.1&#160;million, composed of $1.0&#160;million in gross unrealized appreciation, $30.2&#160;million in gross unrealized depreciation and approximately $30.3&#160;million relating to the reversal of prior period net unrealized depreciation as investment gains and losses were realized. This includes net unrealized appreciation of approximately $3.9&#160;million resulting from reductions to the cost value of our CLO equity investments representing the difference between distributions received, or entitled to be received, on our investments held in CLO equity subordinated notes and fee notes, of approximately $7.1&#160;million and the effective yield interest income recognized on our CLO equity subordinated notes and the amortized cost adjusted income on our CLO equity fee notes of approximately $3.2&#160;million. The most significant components of the net change in unrealized appreciation during the three&#160;months ended March&#160;31, 2026, were as follows (in millions):</p>

		<p class="Text_ind" style="margin:0;padding:0;border-width:0;font-family:Times New Roman PS Std, serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-variant:normal;font-weight:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:8pt;orphans:2;page-break-after:auto;page-break-before:auto;text-align:left;text-indent:24pt;widows:3;margin-top:8pt;">In the normal course of business, we enter into a variety of undertakings containing a variety of warranties and indemnifications that may expose us to some risk of loss. The risk of future loss arising from such undertakings, while not quantifiable, is expected to be remote. As of March&#160;31, 2026, we did not have any commitments to purchase additional investments.</p>

		<p class="Text_ind" style="margin:0;padding:0;border-width:0;font-family:Times New Roman PS Std, serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-variant:normal;font-weight:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:8pt;orphans:2;page-break-after:auto;page-break-before:auto;text-align:left;text-indent:24pt;widows:3;margin-top:8pt;">On August&#160;22, 2023, we entered into Amendment No. 1 to the Equity Distribution Agreement dated August&#160;1, 2019 with Ladenburg Thalmann&#160;&amp; Co. through which we may offer for sale, from time to time, up to $150.0&#160;million of our common stock through an ATM offering. On August&#160;16, 2024, we entered into an amended and restated equity distribution agreement (the &#8220;Amended and Restated Equity Distribution Agreement&#8221;) with Lucid Capital Markets, LLC and Ladenburg Thalmann&#160;&amp; Co. Inc., as the sales agents, to add Lucid Capital Markets, LLC as an additional sales agent to the Amended and Restated Equity Distribution Agreement. We issued a total of 7,183,267<span class="nobreak"> </span>shares of common stock pursuant to the ATM offering during the three&#160;months ended March&#160;31, 2026. The total amount of capital raised net of underwriting fees and offering costs was approximately $12.3&#160;million during the three&#160;months ended March&#160;31, 2026.</p>

Under the Share Repurchase Program, the Company may repurchase, during the 12<span class="nobreak">-month</span> period commencing on October&#160;30, 2025, up to $25.0&#160;million in the aggregate of the Company&#8217;s outstanding common stock in the open market. The timing, manner, price and amount of any share repurchases will be determined by the Company, in its discretion, based upon the evaluation of economic and market conditions, the Company&#8217;s stock price, applicable legal, contractual and regulatory requirements and other factors. The Share Repurchase Program is expected to be in effect until October&#160;30, 2026, unless extended or until the aggregate repurchase amount has been expended. The Share Repurchase Program does not require the Company to repurchase any specific number of shares, and the Company cannot assure stockholders that any shares will be repurchased under the Share Repurchase Program. The Share Repurchase Program may be suspended, extended, modified or discontinued at any time. During the three&#160;months ended March&#160;31, 2026, no shares were repurchased under the Share Repurchase Program.</p>

		<p class="Text_ind" style="margin:0;padding:0;border-width:0;font-family:Times New Roman PS Std, serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-variant:normal;font-weight:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:8pt;orphans:2;page-break-after:auto;page-break-before:auto;text-align:left;text-indent:24pt;widows:3;margin-top:8pt;">In accordance with the 1940 Act, with certain limited exceptions, as of March&#160;31, 2026, we were only allowed to borrow amounts such that our asset coverage, as defined in the 1940 Act, was at least 150%, immediately after such borrowing. As of March&#160;31, 2026 and December&#160;31, 2025, our asset coverage for borrowed amounts was approximately 177% and 191%, respectively.</p>

		<p class="Text_ind" style="margin:0;padding:0;border-width:0;font-family:Times New Roman PS Std, serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-variant:normal;font-weight:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:8pt;orphans:2;page-break-after:auto;page-break-before:auto;text-align:left;text-indent:24pt;widows:3;margin-top:8pt;">In order to qualify for tax treatment as a RIC, and to avoid corporate level tax on the income we distribute to our stockholders, we are required, under Subchapter M of the Code, to distribute at least 90% of our ordinary income and short<span class="nobreak">-term</span> capital gains to our stockholders on an annual basis.</p>
		<p class="Text_ind" style="margin:0;padding:0;border-width:0;font-family:Times New Roman PS Std, serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-variant:normal;font-weight:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:8pt;orphans:2;page-break-after:auto;page-break-before:auto;text-align:left;text-indent:24pt;widows:3;margin-top:8pt;">To the extent our taxable earnings fall below the total amount of our distributions for that fiscal year, a portion of those distributions may be deemed a return of capital to our stockholders. Thus, the source of a distribution to our stockholders may be the original capital invested by the stockholder rather than our taxable ordinary income or capital gains. Stockholders should read any written disclosure accompanying a distribution payment carefully and should not assume that the source of any distribution is taxable ordinary income or capital gains. The final determination of the nature of our distributions can only be made upon the filing of our tax return. We have until October&#160;15, 2027, to file our federal income tax return for the year ended December&#160;31, 2026.</p>
		<p class="Text_ind" style="margin:0;padding:0;border-width:0;font-family:Times New Roman PS Std, serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-variant:normal;font-weight:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:8pt;orphans:2;page-break-after:auto;page-break-before:auto;text-align:left;text-indent:24pt;widows:3;margin-top:8pt;">We may not be able to achieve operating results that will allow us to make distributions at a specific level or to increase the amount of these distributions from time to time. In addition, we may be limited in our ability to make distributions due to the asset coverage requirements applicable to us as a BDC under the 1940 Act. If we do not distribute a certain percentage of our income annually, we will suffer adverse tax consequences, including possible loss of favorable regulated investment company tax treatment. We cannot assure stockholders that they will receive any distributions.</p>
